chunks: And from him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, who said:

I wrote to the Jurist (peace be upon him) asking him about the clay of the grave: is it placed with the deceased in his grave, is that permissible or not? So he answered, and I read the signature (tawqi'), and from it I copied: 'It is placed with the deceased in his grave and mixed with its perfume, if God wills.'

key_terms.التَّوْقِيعَ: The signature (a specific type of Imam's reply)
key_terms.الْفَقِيهِ: The Jurist (a title for the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to place grave clay with the deceased in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of placing grave clay (turba) with the deceased, specifically linking the practice to the sanctity of Karbala through the chapter's context. The Imam’s response, conveyed via his signature (tawqi'), explicitly permits mixing the clay with embalming perfume (hunut), reflecting the Shia tradition of honoring the dead with sacred earth. This practice underscores the spiritual significance of the Imam's burial place and its tangible connection to the believer's final resting place.
